builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding
summary: The method replaces the single-pass draft generation of feature-level drafters (e.g., EAGLE-style heads) with a drafting pass plus uncertainty-triggered reconsideration passes, run in parallel, whose refined guesses are appended to the draft tree. It requires a co-designed drafter training recipe and an updated serving-time drafting algorithm, so the cost is retraining or fine-tuning the drafter and modifying the inference stack, while claimed latency overhead is negligible. It can fail if the base model lacks an open checkpoint to train the drafter against (ruling out API-only targets), if the workload's token distribution makes uncertainty estimates poorly calibrated, or if the modest single-digit speedup does not justify the engineering and training effort.
rationale: The gains are real but modest and depend on retraining a drafter and modifying the serving path, so the technique merits a scoped pilot on the reader's actual inference workload rather than immediate production adoption.
technique: Uncertainty-guided parallel reconsideration for speculative drafting

claims.statement: The method replaces the single-pass draft generation of feature-level drafters (e.g., EAGLE-style heads) with a drafting pass plus uncertainty-triggered reconsideration passes, run in parallel, whose refined guesses are appended to the draft tree. It requires a co-designed drafter training recipe and an updated serving-time drafting algorithm, so the cost is retraining or fine-tuning the drafter and modifying the inference stack, while claimed latency overhead is negligible. It can fail if the base model lacks an open checkpoint to train the drafter against (ruling out API-only targets), if the workload's token distribution makes uncertainty estimates poorly calibrated, or if the modest single-digit speedup does not justify the engineering and training effort.
The authors report average improvements of 5.3% to 10.2% on acceptance length and 3.5% to 9.2% on end-to-end speedup over feature-level speculative decoding baselines across models and benchmarks.
